_doc: Machine-readable arch FACTS - mirror of planning-constants.md. Reference facts: read directly, or by a rule engine where one is shipped. Keyed by arch (SKU peaks/ridge live in sku.json). Every value is calibratable; recalibrate from trace per roofline-models.md ## Calibration.

gfx942._lds_alloc_granule_note: Per-workgroup LDS allocation granule: WG/CU by LDS = floor(lds_per_cu / roundup(shared, granule)). gfx942 value from lds_min_alloc_bytes; not measured on gfx942 hardware here.
gfx942._sched_interval_note: buffer_load_issue_cyc = the global-load (GR) throughput interval the interleave scheduler spreads MFMA against; the MFMA-per-load ratio = buffer_load_issue_cyc / mfma_cadence_cyc[dtype]. lds_sp_fifo_entries_per_simd_pair x (2 pairs/CU) = ds_reads in flight/CU before the steady ds_read_b*_conflict_free_cyc rate applies (burst model).
gfx942._vgpr_occupancy_basis: compiler-derived (LLVM `; Occupancy:` sweep, ROCm 7.2.1/LLVM 22; reproduce with kernel_workflow/scripts/kernel_tools/amd_occupancy.py --compiler-sweep). Steps are [max_next_free_vgpr, waves_per_simd] -- the LAST VGPR count that still fits that many waves. waves = min(cap, file // (granule * ceil(vgpr/granule))). next_free_vgpr is the ArchVGPR+AGPR COMBINED budget on CDNA.
gfx942._cvt_off_f32_i4_note: Records ROCDL/MLIR BINDING availability (hasattr(rocdl,'cvt_off_f32_i4')), NOT silicon. The instruction IS in the gfx942 ISA -- v_cvt_off_f32_i4_e32 assembles on gfx942/gfx950/gfx1100/gfx1201 alike -- so false here is a wrapper gap reachable via inline asm, never a hardware does-not-lower ceiling.
gfx942._mfma_valu_coexec_note: MFMA co-issues with VALU (MI-calc: v_mfma_f32_16x16x16_f16 = 16 cyc / 12 co-issuable; 32x32x8 = 32 / 28). RDNA WMMA canNOT co-execute at all -- hiding softmax/dequant VALU under the matrix op is a CDNA-only lever.
gfx942._mfma_coexec_window_cyc_note: MI-calc-authoritative for CDNA3 (the calculator covers gfx942 but not gfx950). Note 12 of 16 is NOT interval-minus-8: a window model calibrated on CDNA4's 32-cyc case cannot be carried here by subtracting a constant. This is the number to recalibrate an interleave/co-execution tool with before running it on gfx942.

gfx950._lds_alloc_granule_note: measured gfx950 (occupancy sweep over 37 LDS sizes, one MI350X node, 2026-11): WG/CU by LDS = floor(163840 / roundup(metadata.shared, 1280)); 32768 B fits 4 WG/CU, 54272 B fits 2. Occupancy follows metadata.shared, not the descriptor's group_segment_fixed_size (0 for Triton).
gfx950._lds_sp_fifo_note: Refuted as an 8-entry limit (ATT trace, one MI350X node, 2026-11): one wave issues 16 ds_read_b128 (32 ds_read_b32) back to back and stalls at the 17th; two waves on paired SIMDs 10-14 each; four streaming SIMDs stall on bandwidth. Outstanding LDS-DMA (global_load_lds) does not block ds_read issue. No FIFO depth is recorded.
gfx950._ds_read_stride_note: Strides here are the lane-to-lane byte stride of one ds_read_b128. measured gfx950 (timing microbenchmark, 4 waves/CU, one per SIMD, one MI350X node, 2026-11): stride 16 B 16.3 cyc (conflict-free), 32 B 32.3 (2-way), 64 B 64.2 (4-way), 128 B 128 (8-way). With 1 wave/CU the intervals halve and a 2-way conflict is hidden; the absolute interval also depends on how many SIMDs read at once (ATT trace, same node), so compare against a conflict-free baseline under the same load. Same-address broadcast is conflict-free (timing microbenchmark, same node).
gfx950._sched_interval_note: buffer_load_issue_cyc = sustained per-wave buffer_load_dwordx4 interval when all 4 SIMDs of a CU stream (measured gfx950 ~58 cyc, timing microbenchmark, one MI350X node, 2026-11; the limit is shared per CU, ~15 cyc per load). One wave alone issues a load every ~5 cyc until ~16 are outstanding, then 12-16 cyc. Only dwordx4 measured; gfx942 value not measured. MFMA-per-load ratio = buffer_load_issue_cyc / mfma_cadence_cyc[shape].
gfx950._vgpr_occupancy_basis: compiler-derived (LLVM `; Occupancy:` sweep, ROCm 7.2.1/LLVM 22; reproduce with kernel_workflow/scripts/kernel_tools/amd_occupancy.py --compiler-sweep). Steps are [max_next_free_vgpr, waves_per_simd] -- the LAST VGPR count that still fits that many waves. waves = min(cap, file // (granule * ceil(vgpr/granule))). next_free_vgpr is the ArchVGPR+AGPR COMBINED budget on CDNA.
gfx950._l2_fabric_latency_note: Boundary between mostly-L2-hit and L2-miss average read latency, not the L2-miss latency itself. measured gfx950 (1-wave pointer chase at 2.2 GHz, one MI350X node, 2026-11): L2 hit 201-209 cyc, MALL hit 524-554 cyc, HBM 864-899 cyc (~880). An average above 300 cyc means a material share of misses. gfx942/gfx1250: not calibrated.
gfx950._mfma_coexec_measured_note: measured gfx950 (timing microbenchmark, 1 wave/SIMD, one MI350X node, 2026-11): plain VALU 4 cyc each, TRANS and v_permlane16/32_swap 8 cyc each, packed f32 (v_pk_*_f32) 0 fit and the first adds ~16 cyc; packed f16 co-issues like VALU. f8f6f4 shapes have a ~13 cyc head. 16x16x32 bf16: 16.7 cyc interval, 2 VALU fit.
gfx950._mfma_coexec_window_cyc_note: PER SHAPE, not per arch: window = issue interval - head read phase. Keyed by MFMA shape because sizing a 16-cyc shape with a 32-cyc shape's window over-fills every one of them. The 32-cyc interval is CDNA4-ISA-PDF-derived (PASS=4 x 8 passes); the ~8-cyc head phase and the coexec_issue_cost_cyc classes are BEHAVIOUR read off an ATT instruction trace, not documented mechanism -- re-derive on your own shape. gfx942's counts come from a different, authoritative source (MI-calc) and are NOT interval-minus-8, so do not compute one arch's window from the other's. HOW to re-derive rather than take these on faith: an ATT instruction trace timestamps every issue, so both the per-class cost and whether a given op landed inside a shadow or outside it are readable directly off a trace of your own kernel -- which is the same evidence these numbers rest on. The ISA document will never confirm them; it publishes required-NOP hazard tables, not co-issuable cycles.
gfx950._packed_fp32_coexec_note: v_pk_* on f32 canNOT be placed in an MFMA co-execution window at all, while being the cheapest form per element (one issue slot retires two). So packed-vs-scalar is a per-instruction decision: cover-able work scalar, exposed work packed. A blanket scalarize-every-packed-op-in-an-MFMA-block also splits the exposed remainder, which is a straight loss.
gfx950._gws_note: GWS (DS_GWS) is NOT removed on CDNA4 -- ds_gws_init/ds_gws_sema_v assemble on both gfx942 and gfx950; it is removed on RDNA4 (gfx1201 rejects them).

gfx1250._vgpr_occupancy_basis: compiler-derived (LLVM `; Occupancy:` sweep, ROCm 7.2.1/LLVM 22; reproduce with kernel_workflow/scripts/kernel_tools/amd_occupancy.py --compiler-sweep). gfx1250 is its OWN geometry -- neither the CDNA 512/8 nor the RDNA 1536/24 file applies.
gfx1250._note: MI450; wave32 in-kernel (get_warp_size may return 64 - hardcode 32); microarch constants TBD-probe on target

gfx1201._vgpr_occupancy_basis: compiler-derived (LLVM `; Occupancy:` sweep; regenerated unchanged on gfx1201 with ROCm 10 / AMD clang 23.0.0git, llvm-project 8f497e0992fb7513f7f78a6f6b6f1056c375e961, 2026-09-21; reproduce with kernel_workflow/scripts/kernel_tools/amd_occupancy.py --compiler-sweep --arch gfx1201). vgpr_per_wave (256) is the per-WAVE addressable cap, NOT the per-SIMD file -- dividing 256 by a kernel's VGPR count (an earlier hw_budget bug) under-reports RDNA occupancy 2-3x.
gfx1201._dynamic_vgpr_note: LLVM 22/23 llvm-mc -mcpu=gfx1201 accepts `s_alloc_vgpr 8`; do not claim ISA rejection. GEAK has not demonstrated dynamic-VGPR allocation through its HIP/Triton compute paths, so workflow occupancy remains on the compiler-derived static <=256 VGPR/wave model until toolchain evidence proves otherwise.
gfx1201._mfma_valu_coexec_note: RDNA WMMA canNOT co-issue with VALU (MI-calc 'Can co-execute with VALU: False' on rdna3 AND rdna4). Do not port a CDNA 'interleave VALU into the MFMA shadow' plan here.
gfx1201._note: gfx1201 ISA constants; GEAK serving policy covers R9700 and R9600D; calibration is separate. Occupancy-first, no mfma_scaled/blockscale, no TDM; do not apply the CDNA combined-512-VGPR formula (rdna-fork.md).

gfx1200._vgpr_occupancy_basis: compiler-derived (same sweep as gfx1201, measured on gfx1200 itself -- not extrapolated).
gfx1200._note: gfx1200 occupancy geometry only; product mapping and validation are intentionally not inferred from the ISA id.

gfx1151._lds_basis: lds_per_wgp_kib is the value GEAK main carried for this arch, kept because GEAK's default-path amd_ryzen.md tells readers to use it. Basis: the vendor's public GPU architecture specification table lists 128 KiB LDS for this part; the RDNA3 shader ISA reference guide describes the WGP's LDS as one 128 kB array shared by its two CUs and caps one work-group at 64 kB (lds_per_wg_kib). Scope: the per-WGP scope is taken from that RDNA3 model; the LDS chapter of the RDNA3.5 ISA reference guide was not re-read for this entry, so treat the per-WGP scope on gfx1151 as family-derived, not arch-sourced.
gfx1151._vgpr_occupancy_basis: compiler-derived (same sweep, measured on gfx1151 itself).
gfx1151._note: Strix Halo APU (AI MAX 395/495); WMMA _w32, LPDDR-attached -- treat the memory roofline as APU-shared, not discrete-GPU HBM

gfx1100._lds_basis: 128 KiB/WGP and the <=64 KiB/work-group allocation limit are both stated by the RDNA3 shader ISA reference guide (linked from rdna-fork.md), which describes the WGP's LDS as one 128 kB array built from two 64 kB blocks, one per CU, and caps a single work-group at 64 kB. Corroborated by the vendor's public GPU architecture specification table, which lists 128 KiB LDS for this part (the same column reads 64 for gfx942 and 160 for gfx950, i.e. it carries the size of one LDS instance and does not itself name the granularity -- the per-WGP scope comes from the ISA guide). NOT inferred from gfx1201.
gfx1100._vgpr_occupancy_basis: compiler-derived (same sweep, measured on gfx1100 itself).
